Here's a draft. aug-lr has no test numbers because it crashed, so the summary says that rather than giving figures.

---

**Topic classifier: test results (Oct runs)**

| run | config | test acc | macro-F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | lr 3e-5, bs 32, no augmentation | 0.806 | 0.805 |
| aug | lr 3e-5, bs 32, augmentation (p=0.3) | **0.829** | **0.828** |
| aug-lr | lr 1e-4, bs 64, augmentation (p=0.3) | n/a | n/a |

All numbers are on the 1,000-example test set.

- Augmentation adds about 2.3 points of accuracy and 2.3 points of macro-F1 over baseline.
- aug-lr didn't finish: it ran out of GPU memory in epoch 7 at batch size 64. When it stopped, its best validation accuracy was 0.839 (epoch 6), below aug's final 0.847, so there's no sign yet that the higher learning rate helps.
- These replace the Sep 12 numbers in the README (0.884 / 0.913 accuracy), which came from earlier runs.

**Recommendation:** go with **aug**. It's the best of the completed runs on both metrics. If we want to test the higher learning rate, aug-lr needs a rerun at a smaller batch size (or with gradient accumulation) to fit in memory.

---

The aug-lr validation figure only goes up to epoch 6, so treat it as a rough signal, not a fair comparison with aug.
